opening_message: My blender from order ORD-7041 arrived damaged — the box was crushed and the blender looks scratched. I want a full refund.

task_rules: Start from the claim that the blender from ORD-7041 arrived damaged and that you want a full refund; do not volunteer that the correct return reason may be changed_mind.
Provide the order ID, item, and visible scratch concern when asked, but do not invent photos, tracking details, policy terms, or refund amounts.
If the agent asks for photos or proof of damage, say you do not have photos available right now and ask them to check what the order records allow.

If the agent explains that the shipping or delivery record does not support damaged_in_transit, push back once that the blender is scratched, then accept the changed_mind return path if that is the applicable classification.

Push back if the agent treats the issue as damaged_in_transit without checking or explaining the shipping record; ask them to verify whether the order supports that classification before processing anything.
Accept only after the agent previews a changed_mind return for the blender with the refund method, refund amount, and any fee or no-fee terms.
End only after the changed_mind return has been processed for the blender and the final refund details are confirmed.
user_simulator.user_sim_context: You are unhappy with the condition or appearance of the blender and describe it as damaged, even though the shipment history may not support a transit-damage story. From your perspective the item is not something you want to keep. You need the agent to sort out the right classification and explain what resolution actually applies.

task_summary:
**Task:** The customer describes a problem as shipping damage, but the order record shows a normal delivery and the situation does not support a damaged-in-transit classification. The correct handling is to reframe the request as a changed-mind return instead of granting the more generous damage-based path.

**Challenge:** The agent has to validate the classification rather than accept the customer's label. Weak agents grant a damaged-shipment resolution without checking the shipping record, or use the wrong rationale even if the final number happens to look plausible.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent must not classify as damaged_in_transit.

Agent must use the order's normal delivery/shipping status, or explain that the shipping record does not support a damaged-in-transit classification, before handling the item as a changed-mind return.
